name: Ace of Pentacles
symbols: A hand from a cloud holds a coin — the opportunity, given.
A garden below — the ground where the seed will fall.
An arch of foliage — a passage, a way through.
Mountains in the distance — the goal the seed will eventually reach.

reading.upright: The Ace of Pentacles is the material beginning: the offer, the seed, the opportunity that can be taken up.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the opportunity is missed or refused: the seed unplanted, or the scarcity that will not risk the ground.

elementalRegister.value: Earth (Pentacles; the coin, the garden, the mountains)
elementalRegister.note: The Ace of Pentacles is the root of the earth suit: the material beginning, the seed of prosperity that can be planted in the ground.

numericalDegree.note: The Ace is the root of the suit, the seed of the element. It is the degree of pure potential, before the number has begun to differentiate.

courtFunction.note: The Ace is not a court card; it is the elemental root of the suit.

figureType.value: A hand from a cloud, holding a coin
figureType.note: The hand is the only figure. It comes from the cloud, marking the opportunity as a gift from beyond the self.

posture.value: The hand holds the coin upright
posture.note: The upright posture of the coin is the posture of potential: the opportunity is held aloft, ready to be planted.

gesture.value: Holding the coin, above a garden
gesture.note: The gesture is one of offering and planting. The coin is held above the garden, ready to be placed in the ground.

gaze.note: There is no gaze. The Ace is not a personality; it is a force.

movementDirection.note: There is no directional movement. The Ace is the point of opportunity, not the journey.

centralObject.note: The coin is the opportunity; the garden is the ground where it can be planted. Both are the symbols of the card's beginning.

heldObject.note: The coin is held by the hand from the cloud. It is the gift of the element.

creature.note: There is no creature. The Ace is the pure element, before it has taken animal form.

tool.note: The tool is the coin, the instrument of the earth suit.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The Ace's law is the opportunity itself, not a written instruction.

landscape.value: A garden with an arch of foliage, and mountains in the distance
landscape.note: The landscape is the garden, the ground where the seed will be planted, and the mountains, the goal it will reach.

architecture.note: The arch is the architecture of the passage. It marks the way through, the path that the opportunity will take.

threshold.note: The cloud is the threshold between the unseen and the seen. The hand emerges from it, bringing the opportunity into the world.

celestialBody.note: The clouds are the celestial source of the gift. The opportunity comes from above, not from the earth.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The Ace is the clear moment of opportunity.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the hand from the side, the garden below)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The Ace is a point of departure, not a balance.

repetitionCount.note: The number one is the number of the opportunity. The Ace is the single point of beginning.

verticalAxis.value: The hand from above, the garden below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the celestial (the cloud) to the earthly (the garden). The coin is the point of connection.

horizontalAxis.value: The coin held to the side
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the offering: the coin is held out, available to be planted.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The Ace is upright and open.

clothing.note: There is no clothing. The Ace is the bare element, without the mediation of culture.

nudity.note: There is no body. The Ace is the element itself, not a person.

crown.note: There is no crown. The Ace is the root of the suit, not a figure of authority.

wound.note: There is no wound. The Ace is pure potential, not yet marked by experience.

binding.note: There are no chains. The opportunity is free.

water.note: There is no water. The Ace of Pentacles is the root of earth.

fire.note: There is no fire. The Ace of Pentacles is the root of earth.

vegetation.value: The garden and the arch of foliage
vegetation.note: The vegetation is the garden, the ground where the seed will be planted. It is the world of growth and material prosperity.

stone.note: Stone is present as the mountains, the goal that the seed will eventually reach.

polarity.note: The Ace of Pentacles' remedy-pair is the Ace of Swords: earth and air, grounding and clarity. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Ace of Pentacles' material opportunity is the Ace of Swords' clarity: sometimes the opportunity needs to be corrected by the clear sight.

prescribedAct.value: Plant one seed today — a small, material commitment — and let it begin to grow.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of grounding. The Ace of Pentacles' lesson is that the opportunity is not the harvest; it is the seed that must be planted.

detailedReading: The Ace of Pentacles is the root of the earth suit: the material beginning, the seed of prosperity. Its elemental register is earth, and its numerical degree is the Ace, the seed of the element. The figure is a hand from a cloud, holding a coin, above a garden with an arch of foliage and mountains in the distance. The landscape is the garden, the ground where the seed will be planted. There is no creature, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the Ace is the pure element, free and open. The asymmetry of the composition marks it as a point of departure. The prescribed act follows from this: plant one seed today — a small, material commitment — and let it begin to grow. The remedy is clarity — the Ace of Swords — because the opportunity needs to be corrected by the clear sight.

name: Two of Pentacles
symbols: A figure juggles two coins within an infinity loop — the balance is active, not static.
Ships ride high waves behind — the world is moving, and the juggling is in response.
One foot lifted — readiness, the constant adjustment of the stance.
A tall hat — the performance, worn lightly.

reading.upright: The Two of Pentacles is active balance: juggling the demands, adjusting as things move, staying light on the feet.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the juggle fails: overextension, the dropped ball, or the disorganisation that the balance was hiding.

elementalRegister.value: Earth (Pentacles; the juggled coins, the moving ships)
elementalRegister.note: The Two of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of balance. The juggled coins mark it as the card of active, moving balance.

numericalDegree.note: Two is the number of polarity and pairing. The card is the moment at which the single seed of the Ace becomes the paired demands of the Two.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Two is the first differentiation of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: A standing human figure, juggling two coins within an infinity loop
figureType.note: The figure is human and in motion. His juggling marks the card as one of active balance, not static stability.

posture.value: Standing, one foot lifted, body in motion
posture.note: The posture is one of active balance: the figure is moving, adjusting, not still.

gesture.value: Juggling the two coins within the infinity loop
gesture.note: The gesture is one of juggling. The coins are moving, the loop is the shape of the balance.

gaze.value: Looking at the coins or outward
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the juggler. The figure is looking at the coins, not at the ships.

movementDirection.note: The movement is circular. The card is the active balance of the juggle, not the still stability of the ground.

centralObject.value: The two coins and the infinity loop
centralObject.note: The coins are the objects of the juggle; the loop is the shape of the balance. Together they mark the card as one of active balance.

heldObject.note: The coins are held, in motion, not resting. The holding is the holding of the juggle.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human balance, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the juggle: the coins in motion.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The balance is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A sea with ships riding high waves
landscape.note: The landscape is the sea and the ships. The ships ride high waves, marking the world as one in motion.

architecture.note: There is no architecture. The card is the open sea and the moving ground, not the household.

threshold.note: There is no threshold. The card is the balance, not the crossing.

celestialBody.value: The infinity loop (the only celestial mark)
celestialBody.note: The loop is the only celestial mark. It is the sign of the limitless balance.

weather.note: The weather is choppy. The card is the rough day of the juggle.

symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the juggle, though not the balance of the still.

repetitionCount.note: The number two is the number of the pairing. The two coins mark the card as one of the paired demands.

verticalAxis.value: The infinity loop above, the sea below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the loop to the sea. The loop is the sign of the balance, the sea is the world in motion.

horizontalAxis.value: The coins in motion across the figure
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the juggle: the coins are in motion across the figure.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figure is upright, in motion.

clothing.value: A tall hat, motley or festive dress
clothing.note: The tall hat marks the performance; the festive dress marks the figure as one who is at ease in the juggle.

nudity.note: The figure is clothed. His balance is mediated by his ordinary dress.

crown.value: A tall hat, not a crown
crown.note: There is no crown. The figure is not a ruler; he is a juggler.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of balance, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figure is free to move.

water.note: Water is present as the sea. It is the world in motion, the reason for the juggle.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of earth, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the sea, not of the garden.

stone.note: There is no stone. The card is a card of the moving sea, not of the castle.

polarity.note: The Two of Pentacles' remedy-pair is the Two of Swords: earth and air, active balance and stalemate. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Two of Pentacles' juggle is the Two of Swords' decision: sometimes the balance needs to be corrected by the willingness to choose.

prescribedAct.value: Drop one ball today, and see whether the juggle actually needed it.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of letting go. The Two of Pentacles' lesson is that the balance is not the same as carrying everything.

detailedReading: The Two of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of balance. Its numerical degree is two — the number of polarity and pairing — and the figure is a standing man, one foot lifted, juggling two coins within an infinity loop, with ships on the high waves behind. The landscape is the sea and the ships: the world is in motion, and the juggle is the response. There is no creature, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human balance, not of instinct, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the juggle. The prescribed act follows from this: drop one ball today, and see whether the juggle actually needed it. The remedy is decision — the Two of Swords — because the balance needs to be corrected by the willingness to choose.

name: Three of Pentacles
symbols: A mason works on a cathedral arch — skill applied to something larger than the worker.
A monk and a nobleman consult — collaboration across different stations.
Plans held in hand — design, thought before the making.
Three coins carved into the arch — the work itself is the reward.

reading.upright: The Three of Pentacles is craft in collaboration: skilled work, joined with others, making something that none could make alone.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the collaboration falters: teamwork issues, unrecognised skill, or work that has been done without the plan.

elementalRegister.value: Earth (Pentacles; the carved arch, the coins)
elementalRegister.note: The Three of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of craft. The carved arch and the coins mark it as the card of skilled collaboration.

numericalDegree.note: Three is the number of creation and fruition. The card is the moment at which the balance of the Two becomes the craft of the Three.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Three is the first fruition of the suit's energy, in its collaborative form.

figureType.value: A standing mason at work, with two consulting figures
figureType.note: The mason is the figure of the craft; the monk and the nobleman are the figures of the consult. The three together mark the card as one of collaboration across different stations.

posture.value: Standing at the arch, hands at work; the others standing and consulting
posture.note: The posture is one of work and consult: the mason is at the arch, the others are at the plans.

gesture.value: The mason's hands on the arch; the others gesturing over the plans
gesture.note: The gesture is one of shared making. The mason's hands are at work, the others' are on the plans, marking the card as one of collaboration.

gaze.value: The mason at the arch; the others at the plans
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the shared work. The mason is looking at the work, the others at the design.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the craft.

centralObject.value: The cathedral arch and the coins
centralObject.note: The arch is the central object, the work itself. The coins carved into the arch mark the card as one of the craft that is the reward.

heldObject.value: The plans and the mason's tools
heldObject.note: The plans are held by the consulting figures; the tools are held by the mason. The holding is the holding of the craft.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human craft, not of instinct.

tool.value: The mason's tools and the plans
tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the craft: the mason's tools and the designer's plans.

writtenWord.note: The plans are present as drawings. The card is a card of the design, not of the written law.

landscape.note: The landscape is the cathedral interior, the place of the shared making. The card is the build, not the finished building.

architecture.note: The arch is the architecture of the craft. It is under construction, marking the card as one of the making, not the made.

threshold.note: The arch is the threshold between the outside and the inside, the made and the making. The figures are at it.

celestialBody.note: There is no celestial body. The craft is ordinary, not cosmic.

weather.note: There is no weather. The card is the interior of the craft.

symmetry.value: Balanced (the three figures around the work)
symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the collaboration.

repetitionCount.note: The number three is the number of fruition. The three coins mark the card as one of the shared craft.

verticalAxis.value: The arch above, the figures below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the arch to the figures. The arch is the work, the figures are the makers.

horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the collaboration: the figures are around the work.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figures are upright at the work.

clothing.value: The mason's working clothes, the monk's robe, the nobleman's rich dress
clothing.note: The varied dress marks the figures as different stations, working together. The card is a collaboration across different roles.

nudity.note: The figures are clothed. Their craft is mediated by their social positions.

crown.note: There is no crown. The card is a card of collaboration, not of authority.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of craft, not of suffering.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figures are free to collaborate.

water.note: There is no water. The card is a card of earth, not of water.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of earth, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the interior, not of the garden.

stone.note: Stone is present as the cathedral arch, the material of the craft.

polarity.note: The Three of Pentacles' remedy-pair is the Three of Cups: earth and water, craft and celebration. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Three of Pentacles' craft is the Three of Cups' celebration: sometimes the craft needs to be corrected by the willingness to celebrate the work.

prescribedAct.value: Share one piece of work today with someone whose skill is different from yours, and see what it becomes.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of collaboration. The Three of Pentacles' lesson is that the craft is not the solitude; it is the shared making.

detailedReading: The Three of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of craft. Its numerical degree is three — the number of creation and fruition — and the figures are a mason at the cathedral arch, with a monk and a nobleman consulting the plans, and three coins carved into the arch. The landscape is the cathedral interior under construction. There is no creature, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human craft, not of instinct, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the collaboration. The prescribed act follows from this: share one piece of work today with someone whose skill is different from yours, and see what it becomes. The remedy is celebration — the Three of Cups — because the craft needs to be corrected by the willingness to celebrate the work.

name: Four of Pentacles
symbols: A figure holds a coin to the chest — the thing being protected.
One coin on the crown, two under the feet — holding on, in every direction.
A city behind — the security the hoard is meant to buy.
The posture is closed — the body is the vault.

reading.upright: The Four of Pentacles is holding on: security, saving, the willingness to keep what has been earned.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the holding becomes either greed or release: the grip that will not open, or the letting go that frees the hand.

elementalRegister.note: The Four of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of holding. The coins held in every direction mark it as the card of security and the closed grip.

numericalDegree.note: Four is the number of structure and stability. The card is the moment at which the craft of the Three becomes the hoard of the Four.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Four is the stabilization of the suit's energy, in its held form.

figureType.value: A seated human figure, holding a coin to the chest, with coins at the head and feet
figureType.note: The figure is human and closed. His posture marks the card as one of holding, not of giving.

posture.value: Seated, arms drawn in, holding the coin to the chest
posture.note: The posture is one of protection: the figure is closed, holding, guarding the coin.

gesture.value: Holding the coin to the chest
gesture.note: The gesture is one of guarding. The coin is held to the chest, marking the card as one of the held security.

gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the guard. The figure is looking at the world, watching for what might take the coin.

movementDirection.note: There is no movement. The card is the still point of the holding.

centralObject.note: The coins are the central objects, the hoard that is being held. They are held in every direction, marking the card as one of the total hold.

heldObject.value: One coin at the chest, one on the crown, two under the feet
heldObject.note: The coins are held in every direction. The holding is the holding of the total security.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human holding, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tools are the instruments of the holding: the coins in every direction.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The holding is enacted, not written.

landscape.note: The landscape is the city, the world that the hoard is meant to buy. The city is behind, marking the card as one of the security in the world.

architecture.note: The city is the architecture of the world. It is behind, marking the card as one of the held position in the world.

threshold.note: There is no threshold. The card is the holding, not the crossing.

celestialBody.note: There is no celestial body. The holding is ordinary, not cosmic.

weather.note: The weather is fair. The card is the calm day of the holding.

symmetry.note: The composition is balanced. The card is the balance of the total hold.

repetitionCount.note: The number four is the number of structure. The four coins mark the card as one of the total hold.

verticalAxis.value: The coin on the crown, the coins under the feet
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis is the axis of the holding: the coin is above, the coins are below, the coin is at the chest.

horizontalAxis.value: The figure holds the coin to the chest
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the chest: the figure holds the coin to the body.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figure is upright and closed.

clothing.note: The rich robe marks the figure as one of wealth; the crown marks the figure as one of authority. The card is the hoard of the wealthy.

nudity.note: The figure is clothed. His holding is mediated by his ordinary dress.

crown.value: A crown, with a coin on it
crown.note: The crown is the mark of authority. The coin on it marks the card as one of the hold on the authority as well as the wealth.

wound.note: There is no wound. The card is a card of holding, not of suffering.

binding.value: Absent (the closed posture is the binding)
binding.note: There are no chains, but the closed posture is the binding. The card is the self-imposed hold.

water.note: There is no water. The card is a card of earth, not of water.

fire.note: There is no fire. The card is a card of earth, not of fire.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the city, not of the garden.

stone.note: Stone is present as the city, the architecture of the world.

polarity.note: The Four of Pentacles' remedy-pair is the Four of Wands: earth and fire, holding and celebration. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Four of Pentacles' holding is the Four of Wands' celebration: sometimes the hold needs to be corrected by the willingness to share.

prescribedAct.value: Let go of one coin today, and see whether the security actually needed it.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of release. The Four of Pentacles' lesson is that the hold is not the same as the security.

detailedReading: The Four of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of holding. Its numerical degree is four — the number of structure and stability — and the figure is a seated man, holding a coin to the chest, with a coin on the crown and two coins under the feet, and a city behind. The landscape is the city, the world that the hoard is meant to buy. There is no creature, no written word, no wound, and no binding: the card is a card of human holding, not of instinct, not of suffering, and not of restraint. The closed posture is the binding of the card. The symmetry of the composition confirms that it is the balance of the total hold. The prescribed act follows from this: let go of one coin today, and see whether the security actually needed it. The remedy is celebration — the Four of Wands — because the hold needs to be corrected by the willingness to share.

name: Five of Pentacles
symbols: Two figures in the snow — hardship, endured.
A lit stained-glass window above them — help is available, but not seen.
One figure on crutches — the body is bearing the cost.
Five coins in the window — the resource that is there, behind the glass.

reading.upright: The Five of Pentacles is material hardship: loss, exclusion, the cold that has to be walked through.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the hardship begins to lift: help arrives, the door opens, and the return to warmth begins.

elementalRegister.value: Earth (Pentacles; the snow, the stained-glass window)
elementalRegister.note: The Five of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of hardship. The figures in the snow mark it as the card of material loss and exclusion.

numericalDegree.note: Five is the number of the human figure and of disruption. The card is the moment at which the holding of the Four breaks into the hardship of the Five.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Five is the disruption of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: Two human figures in the snow, one on crutches
figureType.note: The figures are human and cold. Their poverty marks the card as one of material hardship.

posture.value: Walking through the snow, hunched, one on crutches
posture.note: The posture is one of hardship: the figures are hunched, walking, bearing the cost.

gesture.value: Arms drawn in, one on crutches
gesture.note: The gesture is one of endurance. The arms are drawn in against the cold, marking the card as one of the endured hardship.

gaze.value: Looking down or at the ground
gaze.note: The gaze is the gaze of the cold. The figures are looking at the ground, not at the window.

movementDirection.value: Forward, slowly (the figures walk through the snow)
movementDirection.note: The movement is forward, but slow. The card is the walking through the hardship, not the arrival.

centralObject.value: The stained-glass window with five coins
centralObject.note: The window is the central object, the help that is available but not seen. The five coins in it mark the resource that is there, behind the glass.

heldObject.note: Nothing is held except the crutches. The card is the hardship, not the resource.

creature.note: There is no creature. The card is a card of human hardship, not of instinct.

tool.note: The tool is the crutches, the support of the walking figure. It marks the card as one of the body bearing the cost.

writtenWord.note: There is no text. The hardship is enacted, not written.

landscape.value: A snowy exterior, with a lit stained-glass window
landscape.note: The landscape is the snow and the window. The snow is the hardship, the window is the help that is not seen.

architecture.value: A building with a stained-glass window
architecture.note: The building and the window are the architecture of the help. The window is lit, marking the resource that is there.

threshold.note: The window is the threshold between the cold and the warmth. The figures are outside it.

celestialBody.value: The stained-glass window (the light of the interior)
celestialBody.note: The window is the celestial light of the card. It marks the help that is there, behind the glass.

weather.note: The weather is snowy. The card is the cold day of the hardship.

symmetry.value: Asymmetrical (the figures walking, the window above)
symmetry.note: The composition is asymmetrical. The card is the hardship, not the balance.

repetitionCount.note: The number five is the number of the human figure. The five coins mark the card as one of the resource that is there.

verticalAxis.value: The window above, the figures below
verticalAxis.note: The vertical axis connects the window to the figures. The window is above, the figures are below, and the help is not seen.

horizontalAxis.value: The figures walking through the snow
horizontalAxis.note: The horizontal axis is the axis of the walking: the figures are walking through the snow.

inversion.note: There is no inversion. The figures are upright, though hunched.

clothing.note: The poor clothing marks the figures as ones of poverty, not of the world. The card is the hardship of the excluded.

nudity.note: The figures are clothed. Their hardship is mediated by their ordinary dress.

crown.note: There is no crown. The figures are not rulers; they are the poor.

wound.note: The wound is the central mark of the card. The crutches and the bandage mark the figures as ones who have been injured.

binding.note: There are no chains. The figures are free, though excluded.

water.note: Water is present as the snow. It is the frozen form of the emotion, marking the card as one of the cold.

fire.value: Absent (the window light is the only warmth)
fire.note: There is no visible fire, but the window light is the warmth that is available. The card is a card of the cold that is being walked through.

vegetation.note: There is no vegetation. The card is a card of the snow, not of the garden.

stone.note: Stone is present as the building, the architecture of the help.

polarity.note: The Five of Pentacles' remedy-pair is the Five of Cups: earth and water, hardship and grief. Each is the corrective to the other's excess.

remedy.note: The remedy for the Five of Pentacles' hardship is the Five of Cups' grief: sometimes the hardship needs to be corrected by the willingness to feel the loss.

prescribedAct.value: Look up once today, and see the help that is already lit for you.
prescribedAct.note: The act is the discipline of sight. The Five of Pentacles' lesson is that the help is there; the missing is in the gaze.

detailedReading: The Five of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of hardship. Its numerical degree is five — the number of the human figure and of disruption — and the figures are two poor humans walking through the snow, one on crutches, with a lit stained-glass window above them. The landscape is the snow and the window: the snow is the hardship, the window is the help that is not seen. There is no creature, no written word, and no binding: the card is a card of human hardship, not of instinct, and not of restraint. The wound is the central mark of the card. The asymmetry of the composition marks it as a hardship, not a balance. The prescribed act follows from this: look up once today, and see the help that is already lit for you. The remedy is grief — the Five of Cups — because the hardship needs to be corrected by the willingness to feel the loss.

name: Six of Pentacles
symbols: A merchant holds scales in one hand and gives coins with the other — giving, with fairness.
Two figures kneel to receive — the receivers, in a posture of need.
The scales are balanced — the giving is not arbitrary.
A rich robe on the giver — the source of the giving is secure.

reading.upright: The Six of Pentacles is fair exchange: generosity, charity, the flow of resource from where it is to where it is needed.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the exchange is unequal: strings attached, debt, or the giving that is a way of holding power.

elementalRegister.note: The Six of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of fair exchange. The scales and the coins mark it as the card of generosity and justice.

numericalDegree.note: Six is the number of harmony and balance. The card is the moment at which the hardship of the Five is resolved into the fair exchange of the Six.

courtFunction.note: Not a court card; the Six is the resolved exchange of the suit's energy.

figureType.value: A standing human merchant giving coins, with two kneeling recipients
figureType.note: The merchant is the figure of the giver; the kneeling figures are the figures of the receivers. The three together mark the card as one of fair exchange.

posture.value: The merchant standing, holding the scales; the recipients kneeling
posture.note: The posture is one of exchange: the giver stands, the receivers kneel, marking the card as one of hierarchy in the giving.

gesture.value: The merchant holds the scales and gives coins; the receivers hold their hands out

name: Seven of Pentacles

Seven coins among the leaves — the investment, growing.
The vine is heavy — the growth is real.
The figure is not harvesting yet — the timing is not yet.

reading.upright: The Seven of Pentacles is patient investment: the long growth, the willingness to wait, the assessment of what has been planted.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the waiting has become frustration: the impatience that uproots the vine, or the recognition that this investment will not return.

detailedReading: The Seven of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of patience. name: Eight of Pentacles
symbols: A figure at a workbench, carving a coin — the work, repeated and refined.
Coins already finished hang beside him — the evidence of practice.
A town behind — the world that the craft will enter.
The posture is absorbed — the attention has been given.

reading.upright: The Eight of Pentacles is the practice: the repeated work that builds mastery, the craft that is earned rather than given.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the practice is distorted: perfectionism that will not finish, drudgery that has lost its meaning, or the laziness that will not begin.

elementalRegister.note: The Eight of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of practice. The carved coins and the workbench mark it as the card of repeated craft.

name: Nine of Pentacles
symbols: A figure stands in a garden, at ease — the abundance, earned and enjoyed.
A bird on her gloved hand — the trained instinct, a wild thing now familiar.
A rich robe — the wealth is worn, not hidden.
Nine coins among the vines — the fruit, fully grown.

reading.upright: The Nine of Pentacles is self-sufficiency: the independence that has been earned, and the pleasure of enjoying what one has built.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the independence is hollow: overwork, a dependence disguised as freedom, or the abundance that cannot be enjoyed.

elementalRegister.value: Earth (Pentacles; the garden, the coins, the bird)
elementalRegister.note: The Nine of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of self-sufficiency. The garden and the bird mark it as the card of earned independence and enjoyment.

name: Ten of Pentacles
symbols: An old figure seated, with a family around — the lineage, gathered.
Ten coins arranged in the Tree of Life pattern — wealth, structured.
An arch — the passage between the generations.
Dogs at the old man's feet — loyalty, kept close.

reading.upright: The Ten of Pentacles is legacy: the wealth that outlives the one who built it, the family that carries it forward.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the legacy is broken: financial loss, a family divided, or the short-term that cannot become a future.

elementalRegister.value: Earth (Pentacles; the coins, the arch, the family)
elementalRegister.note: The Ten of Pentacles is the earth element in its phase of legacy. The coins and the arch mark it as the card of the wealth that outlives the one who built it.

name: Page of Pentacles
symbols: A youth holds a coin, looking at it — the opportunity, examined.
A field behind — the ground where the study will be applied.
Mountains in the distance — the goal, still far.
A focused gaze — the willingness to begin at the beginning.

reading.upright: The Page of Pentacles is the beginning of practical learning: the student, the apprentice, the willingness to start small and to study.
reading.reversed: Reversed, the study is unfocused or refused: the opportunity missed, the laziness that will not begin, or the plan that is not a plan.

elementalRegister.note: The Page of Pentacles is the youthful bearer of the earth element. His coin and the field behind him mark him as a creature of practical learning and material beginning.

posture.note: The upright posture is the posture of readiness. The Page is not yet moving, but he is attentive.

gesture.note: The gesture is one of holding and attention. The coin is held, and the Page is examining it.

Rabbits nearby — fertility, the multiplication of what is cared for.
A rich robe and a canopy of leaves — abundance, made habitable.
